title: ML-estimated headroom attribution and dispute workflow for dedicated pool overages
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a robust way to attribute short-duration burst consumption to tenants in dedicated GPU pools when the system performs cross-tenant headroom rebalancing. The goal is to reduce false overage charges, provide explainable attributions, and enable a lightweight customer dispute workflow that can apply retroactive SLA credits when warranted.

Background:
Current meterization uses instantaneous pool-level accounting and a deterministic leaky-bucket that attributes excess to tenants proportionally to observed token rates. This leads to edge cases where transient routing decisions (regional fallback, emergency spillover) and autoscaler churn cause mis-attribution and customer disputes. Existing reconciliation PRs focus on ledger smoothing and post-facto reconciliation but do not provide an estimator that separates system-induced headroom shifts from tenant-driven bursts.

Scope (this ticket):
- Implement an ML-based headroom estimator service that predicts per-tenant available headroom at sub-minute resolution based on historical throughput, model footprint, and recent routing decisions.
- Use the estimator to compute an "attributable burst" score for each overrun event and persist that score in the billing ledger as metadata for auditing and disputes.
- Surface the attribution and a human-readable explanation in the billing export and dispute UI.
- Implement a first-cut dispute workflow that applies provisional SLA credits when attribution confidence is below threshold and a support ticket is opened.

Out of scope:
- Full redesign of pricing model (billing math remains unchanged for now).
- Enterprise legal dispute adjudication (we provide the tooling and provisional credits; finance handles final adjustments).

Proposal:
1) Headroom estimator: a lightweight time-series model (gradient-boosted trees or small temporal CNN) served as a sidecar in the dedicated metering pipeline. Inputs: per-tenant 5/30/300s token rates, model size/kv cache usage, active shard count for pool, recent autoscaler events, routing fallbacks, and per-tenant priority tier. Output: estimated available headroom (tokens/sec) and a confidence score.
2) Attribution rule: when a pool-level burst exceeds reserved throughput, compute for each tenant an attributable amount = min(tenant_observed_tokens, model_estimator_share * overrun), where model_estimator_share is proportional to estimated headroom deficit and tenant recent slope of token usage. Also emit a forensic explanation string (e.g., "High HTTP fallback from region eu-west-1 after node OOM; estimator confidence 0.67 - 70% of overrun assigned to tenant X").
3) Ledger augmentation: append attribution metadata fields (attribution_score, estimator_confidence, explanation, evidence_links) to the existing event stream row for the overrun. These are persisted as strings for audit and exported to CSV/BigQuery.
4) Dispute workflow: when a customer opens a billing dispute referencing a charge with low estimator_confidence (< 0.6) or an explanation containing system-events, auto-create a provisional SLA credit entry (negative line item) and mark it Pending Support Review. Support can approve/reject with final ledger adjustment.

Data model and storage:
- Attribution metadata stored as strings on the existing event stream row: attribution_score ("0.45"), estimator_confidence ("0.72"), explanation (string <= 1024 chars), evidence_links (comma-separated list of URLs).
- No new relational tables for initial rollout; use existing event-sink and BigQuery export for analysis.

Edge cases and rules:
- If estimator_confidence < 0.4, do not auto-assign any tenant-level overage; tag entire overrun as "system-impact; finance review".
- If multiple tenants have identical service patterns, attribution falls back to proportional token-share with ties broken by tenant priority.
- Retries: model sidecar must be idempotent; if estimator is unavailable, fall back to current deterministic attribution and mark explanation "estimator-unavailable".

Migration plan:
- Week 1: Implement estimator training pipeline on historical ledger + routing logs (offline).
- Week 2: Deploy read-only estimator sidecar that annotates overrun events but does not influence billing (observability period).
- Week 3: Turn on ledger augmentation and export annotated events to BigQuery; run reconciliations against historical disputes.
- Week 4: Enable provisional credit path and integrate with support workflow; monitor fraud/abuse metrics.
- Rollback plan: if false credits > threshold (0.5% of revenue), revert provisional credit auto-create and revert to deterministic attribution.

Acceptance criteria:
- Estimator runs at sub-minute latency and annotates >99% of overrun events during read-only period.
- BigQuery exports contain attribution metadata for annotated events.
- Support workflow can view explanation text and apply/reject provisional credits via the console.
- Post-rollout audits show a reduction in valid billing disputes caused by mis-attribution by >= 60% in pilot customers.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for estimator input sanitization and attribution math.
- Replay test: run estimator on 30 days of historical events and compare attribution to deterministic method; review sample of 100 events with SRE/finance for correctness.
- Canary: enable augmentation for one small dedicated pool and one pilot tenant; collect metrics for 72 hours.

Risks and mitigations:
- Model overfit leading to unfair credits: mitigate by conservative confidence thresholds and human-in-loop review for low-confidence cases.
- Increased billing complexity for customers: surface the explanation string and evidence links in billing exports and support UI.
- Performance overhead on metering pipeline: ensure the sidecar is horizontally scalable and add circuit-breaker to avoid tail latency impact.

Rollout notes:
- Pilot customers: select three customers on dedicated pools with recent dispute history; coordinate with CSMs.
- Observability: dashboards for estimator_confidence distribution, provisional credits count, dispute volume, and revenue impact.

Related docs / links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ML+Headroom+Attribution+Draft
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/meters/pull/742
- BigQuery dataset: projects/redwood-prod/datasets/billing_events (annotated_export table)
- Support playbook draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-Dispute-Playbook

acceptance_criteria: Estimator annotates >=99% of overrun events in read-only mode; BigQuery exports include attribution fields; support can file provisional credits from console; pilot customers show >=60% reduction in mis-attribution disputes.
migration_plan: Phase 1 - offline training; Phase 2 - read-only annotation for 2 weeks; Phase 3 - ledger augmentation + export; Phase 4 - provisional credits & support workflow; rollback if false credit rate exceeds threshold.
